description: With data queued in SENSE, an external busy input that is still set when a received transmission and its EOT end time have passed delays the idle, so the idle is DCD-determined: neither LBT rule 1 nor rule 3 applies and LBT_WAIT_TIMER gets lbt_wait_dcd_ms. csma.vdcd_end does not run while the external input is busy.
note: Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for non-ARQ and gets S_BIND_ACCEPTED (A-0041, A-0047); its S_UNIDATA_REQUEST (priority 0 to SAP 5 at 0.0.1.3, U_PDU "hello", no confirmation) is data queued for transmission and produces no SIS output (A-0095, K-0096). The DTS keeps dts.ttd at the earliest TTD in its transmit queue (C-1050). channel_busy true at 1000 with nothing queued: no output (K-0065). The request at 2000 finds the channel busy, so the node waits in SENSE (K-0066). The bytes at 4000 are those of csma-two-node-zero-lbt: a single-segment NON-ARQ-DATA from 0.0.1.3 to this node (C_PDU ID 1, EOT 10, so end 9000) and one from 0.0.1.3 to the broadcast address (C_PDU ID 2, EOT 10), so two-node condition (a) holds over this transmission (K-0068, K-0072); the S_PDUs are for SAP 9, which no client has bound, so no output (A-0235). The burst ends at 6000 but the external input is still busy, so csma.vdcd_end is not started (K-0111, K-0073). The end time 9000 passes with no input. The external input clears at 12000, after DCD and after the EOT end time, so it is the last to clear and the idle is DCD-determined (K-0006): rule 1 does not apply because the end of the transmission did not produce the idle (K-0072), and rule 2 gives lbt_wait_dcd_ms, 30000 ms (K-0070). Compare csma-external-busy-clears-before-eot, where the same transmission gets rule 1. At 42000 the expiry starts CONT_WAIT with the first draw of seed 0, uniform(16) = 15, so 45000 ms.
